newsitem.title: FINLAND: FOCUS-Kemira sees profit up, issues shares.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Kemira sees profit up, issues shares.

text.p: Finnish chemicals group Kemira Oy on Thursday said it expected its 1996 profit to improve on 1995 and announced plans to issue five million new shares and for the Finnish state to reduce its stake in the company.

The group gave the profit forecast in connnection with its eight-month results, which showed January-August profit before extraordinary items and taxes up 17 percent to 612 million markka ($134 million) from 524 million a year earlier.
In 1995 as a whole, the group booked a profit of 721 million markka.
Kemira said it would issue five million new shares and that the state would sell 16 million Kemira shares to investors at home and abroad.
The new share issue would generate about 250 million markka in new capital. The proceeds would be used to expand core business activities through acquisitions or other investments, Kemira said.
The lead managers of the offering have an option to sell an additional three million new Kemira shares and the state has an option to sell a further two million shares.
"The use of the option to increase the number of new shares to be issued would raise the increase in share capital to about 400 million markka," Kemira said.
Kemira gave no details about the subscription period or the issue price. Its shares closed at 52.50 markka on Wednesday, down 0.40.
The Finnish state currently owns 72.3 percent of the shares and is authorised by parliament to lower its holding to 50.1 percent.
The government said in September it planned to cut the state's ownership to around 55 percent, taking into account any new shares to be included in the offering by Kemira.
